elements.element: Audits must be limited to no more than once per 12 months.
elements.evidence: The clause states: “Audits shall be conducted no more than once per 12 months.”

elements.element: Vendor must provide at least 30 days’ advance notice before an audit.
elements.evidence: The clause requires Licensee to permit an audit “within 30 days” after receiving a request. This is a deadline to permit the audit, not a minimum 30-day advance-notice period; an audit could occur sooner.

elements.element: The audit notice must be in writing.
elements.evidence: The audit is triggered by Licensee’s receipt of a “written request” from Licensor.

elements.element: Audits must be conducted during Customer’s business hours.
elements.evidence: The clause requires each audit to occur during “Licensee’s normal business hours.”
The clause specifies “an independent Certified Public Accountant or other Audit Professional.”

elements.element: The auditor must be bound by confidentiality.
elements.evidence: The auditor must be “bound by confidentiality.”

elements.element: Vendor must bear the audit costs by default.
elements.evidence: The clause states that audit costs are borne by Licensor unless the stated exception applies.

elements.element: Any shift of audit costs to Customer must be based on an underpayment, rather than another type of discrepancy.
elements.evidence: The clause shifts costs upon discovery of any “discrepancy,” not specifically an underpayment, so it permits cost shifting for a broader set of findings.

elements.element: The percentage threshold for shifting audit costs to Customer must be more than 5%.
elements.evidence: The clause uses a threshold of “more than five-percent (5%).” The required underpayment basis is assessed separately and is absent.

elements.element: The auditor must have no direct access to Customer’s systems.
elements.evidence: The clause requires the audit to be conducted “without access to Licensee’s systems,” which is more restrictive than prohibiting direct access.

elements.element: Audits must be limited to no more than once per year.
elements.evidence: The rolling limitation of no more than once per 12 months is at least as restrictive as once per year.

elements.element: Vendor must provide at least 15 days’ advance notice before an audit.
elements.evidence: Requiring Licensee to permit an audit within 30 days after a request does not establish any minimum advance-notice period.

elements.element: Vendor must bear the audit costs by default.
elements.evidence: The clause states that audit costs are borne by Licensor unless the stated exception applies.

elements.element: Any shift of audit costs to Customer must be based on an underpayment, rather than another type of discrepancy.
elements.evidence: The clause uses the broader term “discrepancy” and does not require an underpayment.

elements.element: The percentage threshold for shifting audit costs to Customer must be more than 10%.
elements.evidence: The operative threshold is more than 5%, not more than 10%.

result.reason: Neither position is fully satisfied. The clause does not provide a minimum advance-notice period: “within 30 days” is a deadline for Customer to permit the audit, not 30 days’ advance notice and not even 15 days’ advance notice. The cost-shift trigger is also any discrepancy rather than an underpayment; additionally, the 5% threshold fails the fallback’s 10% requirement. The redline is not minimal because it does not reach either complete level and adds an off-site requirement beyond the stated preferred and fallback positions. Unrelated commercial terms remain operative, and no material contradiction is introduced.
